title: Assessment and Audit
outcomes: Apply scrutiny and best judgement assessments.
Apply summary assessment and assessment of unregistered persons.
Apply departmental and special audit provisions.

meta.exam_tip: Tabulate each assessment with trigger, authority and time limit.

concepts.title: Self-assessment and provisional assessment
body: Section 59: every registered person self-assesses tax and files returns. Assessment means determination of tax liability and includes self-assessment, reassessment, provisional, summary and best judgement assessments.

Section 60: where the taxpayer cannot determine value or rate, it may request provisional assessment; the officer orders it within 90 days, the taxpayer executes a bond with security, and final assessment follows within six months (extendable by six months and up to four years by higher authorities).
On final assessment, tax due attracts interest from the original due date; excess paid is refunded with interest under section 56 if not paid within 60 days of the final order.
concepts.analogy: Taxpayers self-assess; provisional assessment helps when value or rate is uncertain.
concepts.work: A new product with uncertain classification can be provisionally assessed.

concepts.title: Scrutiny and best judgement assessment
body: Section 61: the officer may scrutinise returns and seek explanations in Form ASMT-10 within up to 30 days; if accepted, proceedings end (ASMT-12), otherwise demand proceedings follow.

Section 62: if a registered person fails to file returns after notice under section 46 (15 days), the officer makes a best judgement assessment within five years from the due date of the annual return. If a valid return is filed within 60 days of service of the order (extendable by 60 days with an additional late fee of ₹100 per day), the order is deemed withdrawn — though interest and late fee remain payable.
Section 63: assessment of unregistered persons liable to register, or whose registration was cancelled, on best judgement within five years of the relevant annual return due date.
concepts.analogy: Scrutiny asks; best judgement decides when taxpayers stay silent.
concepts.work: Filing a valid return 80 days after a best judgement order cancels it with extra late fee.

concepts.title: Summary assessment and assessment of unregistered persons
body: Section 64: on evidence of tax liability, the officer may, with prior permission of the Additional or Joint Commissioner, make a summary assessment to protect revenue where delay would harm it — even before the taxable person is identified (the person in charge of the goods is then deemed the taxable person).

On application by the taxpayer within 30 days, or on the Additional/Joint Commissioner's own motion if the order is erroneous, the summary assessment order can be withdrawn and proceedings under section 73/74/74A begin.
Summary assessment is exceptional, used for goods in transit or perishable situations.
concepts.analogy: Summary assessment acts fast when revenue is at risk.
concepts.work: Unclaimed goods in transit with no documents can be summarily assessed.

concepts.title: Audit by tax authorities and special audit
body: Section 65: the Commissioner may order audit of a registered person, at its premises or the tax office, after at least 15 working days' notice; it must be completed within three months, extendable by up to six months. Findings are communicated within 30 days, and demands follow if needed.

Section 66: if, during scrutiny, inquiry or investigation, the officer (Assistant Commissioner or above, with Commissioner approval) believes value has not been correctly declared or credit availed is not within limits, considering complexity, he may direct a special audit by a nominated CA or cost accountant, to report within 90 days (extendable by 90).
The taxpayer must be heard on special audit findings; expenses and remuneration are paid by the Commissioner.
concepts.analogy: Departmental audit has three to six months; special audit has 90 plus 90 days.
concepts.work: A complex valuation case can be referred to a cost accountant for special audit.

viva.q: When can a taxpayer seek provisional assessment?
viva.model: When the value of its goods or services, or the applicable tax rate, is uncertain to it.

viva.q: Who is deemed the taxable person in summary assessment where the owner is unknown?
viva.model: The person in charge of the goods.

viva.q: Who can be nominated for special audit?
viva.model: A chartered accountant or cost accountant nominated by the Commissioner.

viva.q: What follows if scrutiny explanation is not satisfactory?
viva.model: Action under sections 61(3) leading to audit, inspection or demand under section 73, 74 or 74A.

viva.q: Who bears the cost of special audit?
viva.model: The Commissioner determines and pays the expenses and remuneration of the auditor.
